/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 27 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3124 (39)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5272 (78)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2292 (34)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1562 (3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 844 (1)
CAPESIZE
It has been a disjointed week with UK holiday on Monday followed by a Singapore holiday today, which has resulted in very little activity in the Pacific. The Atlantic was also reported as quiet with both cargo and tonnage lists rather thin.

There remains positive sentiment in the Atlantic with fixtures trending up from what was reported to be a busy day yesterday. The Dorado (179,842/2011) from Cargill was fixed basis Tubarao to Qingdao 20/24 June at $37.25 to Classic. There were reports of a number of fixtures at $37.50 but nothing was confirmed.

In the Pacific Vale fixed a vessel for Teluk to Qingdao at $10.25 and a Whyalla to Qingdao cargo was fixed to Winking at $23. It was reported that $16.40 was fixed for C5 post index yesterday, slightly up on index.
PANAMAX
Today, the P5TC rose by $311 to settle at $20,629. Market participants report a softer tone in the Atlantic, with a handful of fixtures concluded, at slightly lower levels than previously seen. While some enquiry remains in the market, it is currently insufficient to offset the growing tonnage list. Fronthaul grain and mineral demand is evident, however, brokers note that much of this interest is for forward dates. On the prompt side activity has been said to be thinner with the available tonnage count continuing to expand. In contrast, sentiment in the Pacific remains positive, supported by a higher volume of concluded fixtures and firmer rates. Market sources indicate that export volumes from Australia and Indonesia remain strong, with demand for prompt tonnage still increasing which is reflected in the steady flow of reported fixtures. Period activity is also said to have picked up, with charterers notably seeking coverage for longer durations.

Atlantic
The Crimson Ark (81,765 2016) open in Gibraltar for prompt dates is said to have been place on subjects for a trans Atlantic trip but no further details have emerged.

Asia
Tongli are reported to have taken the Sea Orion (76,602 2005) open Guangzhou in direct continuation for an Indonesian coal stem to South China at $23,000. IMC were said to have covered on subjects their East Kalimantan to Vietnam requirement for 7-10 June. Both the Ningbo Innovation (75,413 2001) and the Cpt Stefanos M (75,213 2008) were reported to have fixed for Indonesia rounds, although no additional details have surfaced. The HC Energy (73,594 2006) open in South China spot was reported to have fixed at $21,000 with no further information reported.
SUPRAMAX
It was another rather lacklustre day from the sector with the widespread holiday in the Indian Ocean and Singapore also being off it was a decidedly mute day from Asia and very little fresh activity surfaced. The Atlantic remained a positional affair, brokers saying that the US Gulf remaining relatively firm with a good supply of fresh enquiry. It surfaced that recently, the Tomini Destiny (63,615 2017) fixed delivery Houston trip to China with grains at $24,500 with Seastar. Also, the Ruby Eternity (63,807 2023) open Newark fixed for trip with coal delivery Baltimore redelivery Thailand at $28,000 with XO Shipping. Elsewhere, from the Continent-Mediterranean there remained a positive tone although some felt a ceiling may have been reached. The 11TC average finished the day up just $29.00 at $19,740.
HANDYSIZE
It was a mixed day of activity, with only minor fluctuations observed across both basins. The BHSI edged up by 1 point to 844, while the 7TC average rose by $25 to $15,194. In the Continent and Mediterranean, activity remained subdued and sentiment remained largely positional, with rates holding in line with previous fixtures. The US Gulf, however, saw fresh demand and increased activity, with rates reflecting a slightly firmer tone. In contrast, the South Atlantic continued to lag, as ample tonnage and limited fresh demand kept downward pressure on rates. Across Asia, the market remained positive, supported by a healthy balance between tonnage availability and cargo demand in key loading regions.

Atlantic
The Nordorinoco (38,040 2015) fixed on voyage terms from the US Gulf to Reunion with wood pellets, but further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The African Harrier (37,707 2014), open Japan in early June fixed for two laden legs at $19,500, and the Pan Optimum (37,704 2020) open WC India also fixed for two laden legs with delivery from Singapore at $18,500 by Norden, but further details were not disclosed. The Daiwan Leader (34,442 2018) open Henderson at the beginning of June was fixed for a trip from WC Australia to Indonesia with alumina at $23,000 by Norden. The Strategic Harmony (39,880 2014) open North China at the end of May fixed a trip south at around $18,000, again lacking further details.

Market Fundamentals
South Africa Truck Shutdown Risks Chrome, Coal Export Flows

South Africa’s chrome and coal export supply chains face potential disruption ahead of a planned nationwide truck drivers’ shutdown on 30 May, McCloskey reports. The industrial action, led by the All Truck Drivers Forum and Allied SA (ATDF-ASA), is expected to target key freight corridors linking mining regions to the Richards Bay and Maputo ports, which collectively process up to 780 trucks daily. Market participants are monitoring risks to bulk commodity logistics and port throughput, particularly along the N3, Ermelo, Middelburg, and Mozambique routes. The protest reflects mounting labour tensions over the employment of foreign drivers, adding uncertainty to regional mineral export flows.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA market was under pressure early on with Jun sold down to 39000, July 33650 and 31650 on the Aug. As stronger Atlantic fixtures were reported over the course of the day, the June rallied up to 40000 and Jul 34050. The Jun v Jul spread continued to widen and strengthen, with 5600 trading in volume. The Q3 and Q4 closed marginally weaker, with significant Jun v Q34 buying appetite. The Q3 was sold down to 32500 and the Q4 31600, together with 900 being sold on the Q3 v Q4 spread. Interest on the Cals was thin today, with a few prints on the C27 between 26600-26700 and 22950-23000 on the Cal28.

ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场延续分化格局，好望角型船运费走强（BCI+78至5272），太平洋市场受假期因素影响成交清淡，大西洋端情绪积极；巴拿马型船P5TC上涨311至20629，太平洋段需求支撑明显，澳印出口活跃；超灵便型与灵便型市场整体平稳，美国海湾需求回暖。

sections.title: 市场结构
sections.content: 假期因素导致亚太市场活动受限，太平洋船舶供给宽松；大西洋端情绪向好，货物与船舶清单双薄；澳大利亚与印尼煤炭出口维持强劲，支撑太平洋地区期租需求；即期船舶供应持续增加，对Atlantic端价格形成压力。

sections.title: 干散货信号
sections.content: Cape 180 5TC即期升水至44314，6月合约贴水结构加深；Panamax 82 5TC突破20000美元，季度合约Q3-Q4呈下降趋势；Supramax 11TC小幅上扬29至19740，前端合约小幅回落；铁矿石与炼焦煤价格持平，焦煤237美元/吨。

sections.title: 交易关注
sections.content: 关注好望角型船大西洋-太平洋价差机会；Panamax太平洋端即期船舶紧张度；FFA曲线前端（Jun）流动性；美国海湾煤炭/谷物进口需求回暖信号；6月合约换月窗口期价差交易。

market_watch: 好望角型船：太平洋假期后成交恢复情况，大西洋装港船舶排队变化
巴拿马型船：澳印煤炭出口量及即期船舶供给紧张度
FFA市场：6月合约持仓变化，Cape/Panamax季度价差交易机会
美国海湾：谷物出口需求及灵便型船舶运费支撑
铁矿石价格：62%澳矿108.8美元/吨，炼焦煤维持237美元/吨

route_focus.view: 图巴朗至青岛航线，好望角型船即期市场参考水平$37.25-37.50/吨，受大西洋装港货盘支撑，但假期后恢复待观察。
太平洋往返航线，巴拿马型船5TC即期报20629美元，澳大利亚印尼煤炭出口强劲支撑需求，即期船舶供给趋紧，租金仍有上行动能。
Skaw-Passero至巴西港口航线，灵便型船38TC报6764美元（+28），美国海湾需求回暖带动大西洋市场情绪改善，南大西洋运力仍显充裕。
